source_refs.note: 4- Termination of replication: a main subheading of 19.3.3 Mechanism of DNA Replication, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 128-128.

blocks.text: The termination of replication occurs at specific sequence of nucleotides called termination site. The region of DNA between the origin site and termination site is termed as a replication unit or replicon. During termination, DNA polymerase I removes the RNA primer and fills in the gap with DNA nucleotides. It also fills any gaps between Okazaki fragments. The enzyme DNA ligase joins the Okazaki fragments of the lagging strand.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: During replication, one strand of the original DNA is conserved, while the daughter strand is synthesized anew. It means that half of the original DNA molecule is conserved in each new generation of DNA.

blocks.alt: One replication fork. Ahead of it gyrase sits on the parental double helix and helicase opens the strands. On the upper arm DNA polymerase III makes the leading strand continuously towards the fork. On the lower arm the lagging strand is made away from the fork as Okazaki fragments, each starting with an RNA primer made by primase; DNA polymerase III extends each fragment, DNA ligase joins them and single-strand binding proteins hold the template open.
